meta.note: A day about who gets credit for a look. Instagram's new wordmark read as craft in one interview and as AI slop in another, while two more pieces argue that the visible human hand is now the point.

stories.title: The EU says a sparkle icon is not an AI label
stories.blurb: New EU guidelines set out when AI labelling is actually required and what that means for AI-powered features and products. The short version is that the sparkle icon everyone reached for is not enough.

sources.name: Smashing Magazine
sources.headline: New EU Guidelines For AI Labelling

stories.title: Clay refuses the geometric default of its own industry
stories.blurb: Working with illustrator and animator Hudson Christie, Clay keeps its identity away from the generic geometric look associated with tech. The stated reason is the aesthetics that AI prompting produces.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: Clay embraces imperfection in the face of AI-prompted aesthetics

stories.title: Ten controversies later, is Framer closing its marketplace?
stories.blurb: A creator who has watched the Framer marketplace evolve walks through its history and ten disputes along the way. Relevant to anyone whose income depends on someone else's platform.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: Framer is killing the marketplace… or are they?

stories.title: Instagram's first refresh in ten years, read two ways
stories.blurb: Creative director Christy Silva and brand design director Cynthia Pratomo walk through the new brand system and wordmark. Elsewhere the same wordmark is called a perfect embodiment of AI slop.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: “Instagram has evolved”: the process and craft behind Instagram's first major refresh in over ten years

sources.name: PRINT Magazine
sources.headline: Instagram Refreshes Its Look for a New Era

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: The new Instagram logo is the perfect embodiment of AI slop

stories.title: Jaguar takes the rebrand fight into the cabin
stories.blurb: The Type 01 interior has been revealed, the follow-up to a Type 00 concept that turned into a culture-war story from December 2024 onwards. One reviewer reads the split cabin as built to troll the critics.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: Jaguar doubles down on its controversial rebrand with a (literally) divisive interior design

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Jaguar's new car's interior has been revealed, welcome to the inside of the Type 01

stories.title: A hand-drawn Spider-Man poster outperforms the official one
stories.blurb: A viral hand-drawn poster is being read as evidence that people want more art and originality in movie advertising. The nickname stuck faster than the studio artwork did.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: Viral hand-drawn Spider-Man poster shows people are craving more originality in movie art

stories.title: Inside an AI generated movie, the best parts were human
stories.blurb: A look at a Higgsfield production about three lads in a London pub fantasising about stardom. The verdict from inside the process is that what works is what people made.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: I looked inside an AI generated movie, and the best parts were all human

stories.title: Two photographers who built the impossible before the shutter
stories.blurb: London's October Gallery pairs Benji Reid and Zana Masombuka, who constructed their imaginative scenes by hand rather than afterwards on a screen. The piece sets that against how most agencies produce a surreal image.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: What artists Benji Reid and Zana Masombuka can teach us about building believable fantasy

stories.title: YouTube's new policy splits animators into two groups
stories.blurb: Established creators may earn more under the change. For everyone else it gets harder.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: YouTube's new policy is bad news for animators

stories.title: Booksellers push back on quiet bulk buying of rare books
stories.blurb: Booksellers suspect AI firms are buying rare books in bulk and destroying them. They are starting to resist the trade.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: Booksellers suspect AI firms are buying and then destroying rare books

stories.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash lands three weeks after 3.6
stories.blurb: Google says the new Flash release carries substantial improvements over a version that shipped three weeks ago. The release cadence is now shorter than most design review cycles.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: Google announces Gemini 3.7 Flash just three weeks after previous release

stories.title: Suno adds MIDI and starts behaving like a DAW
stories.blurb: Studio 2.0 pushes Suno closer to a digital audio workstation instead of a thin editor with generative features. MIDI support is the headline addition.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Suno is trying to look more like a real music production tool
